gates.reason: Checked policy-write capability propagation, SPA-safe rendering, and untrusted session/command values; React text rendering is used and no direct write, credential egress, or injection sink appears.
Checked displayed permission, safety, drift, and prompt-friction claims against their input fields and explicit approximation disclosure; evidence rows retain session, pattern, and command context.
Hot computations are memoized, audit tables are incrementally paged, and risk rows are sorted before paging.
Rendering tests contain no production auth, filesystem, network, secret, or injection path.
Tests assert layout and headings but do not implement detector, parser, arithmetic, provenance, or recommendation logic.
Test-only fixtures and DOM assertions are not a shipped hot path or performance probe.
Filesystem-derived plan names and metrics are rendered through React text nodes; the component performs no filesystem access, write, secret egress, or raw-HTML insertion.
The verdict turns sample cluster percentages into an unsupported generalized shipping-risk claim and hard-coded action thresholds without provenance.
The scatter creates one X-axis tick and SVG grid group for every integer through the maximum file-reference count, allowing input magnitude to drive excessive allocation and DOM size.
Security-relevant tests verify denied enterprise principals cannot access or invoke policy write and that writes require explicit confirmation.
Tests verify the emitted write payload has the permissions wrapper, previews both populated buckets, and reports server success or failure without altering results.
Test-only rendering and mocked calls are not shipped hot-path code or a performance probe.
Checked SPA/server separation, capability gating, confirmation, CSRF-client delegation, and rendering of rules/server messages; no raw HTML or direct filesystem/network bypass appears.
The copied snippet and write payload derive from the same computed diff, omit empty buckets, preview exact selected rules, and preserve server-reported outcomes.
Diff and snippet calculations are memoized and the component introduces no request-loop, ingest, or large-allocation hotspot.

findings.title: Plan verdict presents an unproven recommendation as a reproducible conclusion
findings.what: Lines 364-368 compare current cluster percentages, then assert that long plans are most likely to ship under-specified and prescribe thresholds of approximately six file references or 1,000 words. The component provides neither artifact/field provenance nor a derivation for those thresholds, and it does not qualify the observation with the dataset's collection date. Cluster membership itself uses word count and verification presence, so the broader shipping-risk claim is not established by the displayed arithmetic.
findings.fix: Describe the percentages strictly as an observation of the loaded plan set, show structured provenance and an “as of” date, and remove the shipping-risk/threshold prescription unless those thresholds are derived from cited evidence.
findings.acceptance: Given a fixed PlanSignature fixture, the verdict identifies the source artifact/fields and dataset date, reproduces the displayed percentages, and contains no generalized shipping-risk or 6-file/1,000-word recommendation unless a test verifies its cited derivation.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 340-368 derive only A/C verification percentages and then introduce the causal-sounding risk statement and thresholds. Comparison-only inspection of the baseline parser confirmed its structured inputs are fileRefs, words, sections, and hasVerification; it supplies no shipping outcome, date, or threshold provenance.

findings.title: Scatter tick generation scales with the largest file-reference value
findings.what: Lines 109-116 allocate xMax+1 tick values, and lines 168-192 render a line and text node for each. A single plan with a large fileRefs value can therefore cause a large synchronous allocation and SVG DOM expansion even when only a few plans are displayed.
findings.fix: Use a fixed tick budget (for example 6-10 evenly spaced ticks), clamp pathological numeric inputs, and base grid complexity on the budget rather than xMax.
findings.acceptance: A component test with a plan whose fileRefs is at least 100,000 renders a bounded number of X ticks (no more than the chosen budget), completes without allocation failure, and preserves the plotted point and axis maximum.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed xMax directly determines Array.from length at line 116 and every element becomes an SVG group. Comparison-only inspection of the baseline parser confirmed fileRefs is an input-derived count of numbered lines, so it is not inherently restricted to a small plotting range.
